extra.message: User-controlled `sourcePath` and `format` (from POST body in api/instructor/resources/convert/route.ts) are interpolated directly into an `execSync` shell command. An instructor/TA can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g. format='pdf; rm -rf /').

`importExternalResourceMetadata` fetches an attacker-supplied `sourceUrl` with no validation or blocking of internal/loopback addresses. An instructor can use the server to make requests to internal services (SSRF).
`outputPath` is read directly from the `outputPath` query parameter and passed to `readFile` with no sanitization. Any instructor/TA can read arbitrary files on the server (e.g. /etc/passwd, .env).

Route params `category` and `filename` are concatenated into a filesystem path via `join(...)` with no path validation or normalization. Any authenticated user can traverse the filesystem (e.g. category=../../../../) to read arbitrary server files. There is also no per-file authorization check.

The `category` field (from multipart form data) is interpolated into the upload path via `join`/`mkdir` without sanitization. An authenticated user can supply category='../../<dir>' to write files to arbitrary directories on the server.

`fetchCohortOnboardingPacket` (and `saveCohortOnboardingPacket`) build a file path from `cohortName` without `basename()` sanitization, unlike `fetchRosterSnapshot`. A cohort name containing '../' (set by an admin via the cohort create route) allows reading/writing arbitrary files.

`findStaffByEmail` builds an LDAP/directory filter `(mail=${email})` without escaping the email. It is called from api/instructor/courses/route.ts with user-controlled `staffEmail`, allowing filter injection. Note `verifyDepartmentMembership` correctly escapes, but this path does not.

`resolveSubmissionReturnDestination` returns the raw `x-redirect-url` header value as the redirect destination with no allowlist. An attacker can craft a link that redirects students to an arbitrary external domain after submission (open redirect).
Password reset token is generated with `Math.random().toString(36)` which is not cryptographically secure. An attacker can predict reset tokens and take over accounts.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: `confirmPasswordReset` only checks `record.usedAt` and never verifies `record.expiresAt`, so a password reset token remains valid indefinitely after it is issued.

The iron-session cookie signing key falls back to a hardcoded, publicly-known string when SESSION_SECRET is unset. If deployed without the env var, an attacker can forge session cookies and impersonate any user (including admins).

`recordRejectedResetSubmission` logs the entire raw request body with `console.warn`. The password reset confirm route calls it with the full body, so a rejected new password (and token) is written to application logs in plaintext.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The `document_title` query parameter is interpolated into the `Content-Disposition` header without stripping CR/LF characters, allowing HTTP header injection (response splitting). Contrast with resources/route.ts which sanitizes CR/LF.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: `buildExportErrorResponse` returns the raw error message and full stack trace when the caller passes `detail=full`, exposing internal implementation details and file paths in the export endpoint's error responses.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The discussion POST handler inserts a thread using `body.courseId` without checking `canAccessCourse`, so any authenticated user can create discussion threads in courses they are not enrolled in or assigned to.

The seed script creates all demo accounts (including admin@lms.edu) with the well-known hardcoded password 'password123'. If the seed data is ever used outside a throwaway dev environment, these credentials grant admin access.
